conventions.convention: k is a field; vector-space tensors are over k. Tensor powers are left-associated, V⊗0=k, V⊗1=V, and empty sums are zero. Dropping parentheses is licensed after the coherence lemma.

The injection and quotient-kernel lemma assumes AC, consumed through complements. Coefficient separation inherits that proof assumption in arbitrary ambient dimension; its finite-dimensional case is proved without AC.

Tensor-dual surjectivity is asserted for finite-dimensional V and W. Evaluation has domain V*⊗V; coevaluation sends 1 to Σv_i⊗v_i* in V⊗V*, with the displayed associators and unit identifications in the zigzags.

Presentation base change uses a unital homomorphism between commutative rings. The quotient isomorphism is prescribed by s⊗(y+I)↦(s⊗y)+im(S⊗I); the image, rather than an assumed injection of S⊗I, is used. No flatness is required.

The Coxeter generator set S is finite, but W may be infinite. There is one unit parameter per odd-edge component: R=Z[v_1±1,…,v_c±1], and v_s=v_t for conjugate simple generators. An infinite Coxeter label imposes no braid relation.
The normalized quadratic is T_s²=(v_s−v_s⁻¹)T_s+1. In the decreasing-length multiplication case the coefficient of T_sw is 1; the extra term is (v_s−v_s⁻¹)T_w. T_1 is the empty product.

Multiplicative generators are S_s=v_sT_s with Q_s=v_s², so S_s²=(Q_s−1)S_s+Q_s and T_s=v_s⁻¹S_s. Reversal is R-linear and reverses multiplication; bar preserves multiplication and is semilinear over v_i↦v_i⁻¹.

Odd-dihedral commutation forces equality of parameter differences, not necessarily equality of units. Over an arbitrary commutative ring the condition is (v_t−v_s)(v_t+v_s⁻¹)=0; over an integral domain it gives v_t=v_s or v_t=−v_s⁻¹.

For class-constant specialized units u_s, the generator assignment T_s↦[s] into A[W] is an algebra map exactly when every u_s²=1. Both single-parameter specializations v↦1 and v↦−1 yield the group ring.
Finite module coordinate lists in the matrix lemma start at zero. The determinant clauses apply only for n≥1; n=0 is the zero module with its empty basis.

The regular tensor-power detection statement uses the action on the first factor for left modules and on the last factor for right modules, and asserts detection only for n≥1; no canonical A-action on A⊗0=R is claimed.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated finite Coxeter matrix and generic parameter presentation, there is a unique unital R-algebra homomorphism ρ:H→End_R(E) taking T_s to P_s, with ρ(T_w)(e_1)=e_w. The family (T_w) is an R-basis, ρ is injective, and every commutative base change R→R′ gives the presented specialized algebra with R′-basis (1⊗T_w), without a flatness hypothesis.

For a commutative ring R and set S, R⟨S⟩ is the unital associative R-algebra free as an R-module on finite words, including the empty word, with concatenation multiplication. Every map S→A into an R-algebra extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism. The two-sided ideal generated by E consists of finite sums aeb, and a homomorphism killing E factors uniquely through R⟨S⟩/(E). For a field and a basis-indexed S, this identifies with the tensor algebra.

For a homomorphism R→S of commutative rings, S⊗R R⟨X⟩ is canonically S⟨X⟩ on the prescribed word values. For a two-sided ideal I, S⊗R(R⟨X⟩/I) is canonically (S⊗R R⟨X⟩)/im(S⊗R I) on the prescribed tensor-coset values, without flatness. An R-module basis (a_i) of an R-algebra transports to the S-basis (1⊗a_i).

On E=R^(W), the stated left and right length operators satisfy P_sQ_t=Q_tP_s, P_s²=(v_s−v_s⁻¹)P_s+id and the analogous Q relation, with the displayed inverses. They satisfy all finite braid relations. Reduced P-products depend only on w and take e_1 to e_w. W need not be finite.

Reduced products define T_w independently of the reduced expression, with T_1=1. On both sides, multiplying by T_s gives T_sw or T_ws in the increasing-length case and adds (v_s−v_s⁻¹)T_w in the decreasing-length case. The T_w span H; independence and freeness are not asserted here.

For a commutative ring R and n≥0, the finite multivariate polynomial ring and the finite-support Laurent ring Λ_R,n have their stated monomial R-bases and substitution universal properties; Laurent substitution uses units. Both are domains when R is a domain. Over a domain, numerator-denominator pairs with nonzero denominator give the stated fraction fields and injective embeddings.

H is the quotient of the free associative R-algebra by (T_s−v_s)(T_s+v_s⁻¹) and all finite braid relations, where R is the Laurent ring with one unit parameter per odd-edge component. It has the stated presented-algebra universal property. Two simple generators are conjugate in W if and only if they belong to the same odd-edge component.

H has the unique R-algebra reversal anti-involution T_w#=T_w⁻¹ indexed by the inverse group element, explicitly T_w#=T_{w^{-1}}. Each T_s is a unit with inverse T_s−(v_s−v_s⁻¹). The involutive semilinear bar sends v_i to v_i⁻¹ and T_w to the inverse of T_{w^{-1}}. S_s=v_sT_s satisfies (S_s−v_s²)(S_s+1)=0.

For k-vector spaces, the named canonical associators, symmetries and unit isomorphisms satisfy naturality, the pentagon, unit triangle and both symmetry hexagons, with exactly the map domains and composites displayed in Statement (1)–(5). These are equalities of k-linear maps on the whole iterated tensor products.

For finite-dimensional k-vector spaces V,W, the canonical map V*⊗W*→(V⊗W)* is an isomorphism taking the dual product basis to the product dual basis. The tensor Σv_i*⊗v_i is the basis-independent preimage of id_V under Hom–tensor duality. Evaluation and coevaluation are basis-independent and satisfy both displayed zigzags.
Assuming AC, tensoring an injective k-linear map f with id_W is injective. For subspaces U⊆V and Z⊆W and quotient maps p,q, the identified tensor subspaces satisfy ker(p⊗q)=U⊗W+V⊗Z.

alerts.finding: The Definition permits an arbitrary unital ring R and says: “The map x↦e_x is the standard basis inclusion.” For the zero ring and X with two distinct elements, every e_x is the same zero tuple, so this map is not injective. The indexed-family construction remains usable in the owned proofs, which do not require this inclusion claim.

The Definition first requires “M≠0 and its only submodules are 0 and M”, then says: “Equivalently, M has no proper nonzero submodule.” The zero module satisfies the second clause but fails M≠0, so the asserted equivalence is false as written. The owned finite-module proof uses the nonzero simple-module condition.

seams_checked.note: The consumed clauses retain finite S and potentially infinite W. Reduced-word F1 quotes Matsumoto braid connectivity; operator F1 quotes length ±1 and exchange, F3 quotes ambient dihedral reducedness, and F4 quotes braid connectivity. The S3 example uses the type-A identification with transported labels and inversion length. Exact dihedral order is supplied by the dihedral/Matsumoto results, not inferred from the presentation definition alone.

The citing page names this as a prerequisite but attributes no tensor/descent proposition to it. Its six item dependency lists contain no owned batch-1 supplier. Thus this is a contextual page edge, with no strengthened mathematical quotation found.
